'''Nicola Jane Spence''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE}} (born 22 February 1961<ref>{{cite news| title =Profile – Professor Nicola Spence: Growing concerns that give an academic grounding in business|work=Greg Wright | date =5 January 2010 | url =https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/profile-professor-nicola-spence-growing-concerns-that-give-an-academic-grounding-in-business-1-2318721 }}</ref>) is the [[Chief Plant Health Officer]] and [[Civil Service (United Kingdom)#Grading schemes|Deputy Director]] for plant and bee health at the [[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs]].

==Early life and education==
Spence was educated at [[The Mount School, York]] and [[Bridlington School]].<ref name=yorkp>{{cite news| title =Professor Nicola Spence appointed as Science City York's new chief executive | work =Ron Godfrey | publisher =[[The Press (York)|The Press]] | date =15 September 2009 | url =http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/4628862.Professor_Nicola_Spence_appointed_as_Science_City_York___s_new_chief_executive/ }}</ref> She obtained a BSc degree in [[Botany]] from the [[University of Durham]].<ref name=BSPP>{{cite web |url=http://www.bspp.org.uk/profiles/spence.php |title=Professor Nicola Spence – BSPP Vice President |access-date=19 May 2018 |date=January 2018 |publisher=[[British Society for Plant Pathology]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520192738/http://www.bspp.org.uk/profiles/spence.php |archive-date=20 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Before starting her [[Master's degree]], Spence volunteered at the Bermuda Marine Biology Research Institute then worked as a [[tutor]] for [[O level]] and [[A level]] students, and was unsure whether she wanted to pursue a career in research.<ref name=birk>{{cite web |url=http://www.bbk.ac.uk/study/profile-selector?pid=nicola-spence |title=Nicola Spence |access-date=19 May 2018 |publisher=[[Birkbeck College]]}}</ref> Spence undertook an MSc degree in Microbiology from [[Birkbeck College]],<ref name=BSPP /> which she states 'turned out to be the best decision I made at the start of my career.'<ref name=birk /> Spence then obtained a PhD degree in [[Plant Virus|Plant Virology]] from the [[University of Birmingham]];<ref name=BSPP /> her thesis was entitled ''The identification, distribution and ecology of bean common mosaic virus in Africa''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Spence |first=Nicola |year=1992 |title=The identification, distribution and ecology of bean common mosaic virus in Africa |type=PhD |publisher=University of Birmingham }}</ref>

In December 2018 Spence represented the University of Birmingham on the Christmas edition of ''[[University Challenge]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/latestnews/2018/christmas-university-challenge?ns_campaign=bbc_press_office&ns_linkname=corporate&ns_mchannel=social |title=Christmas University Challenge alumni line-up announced |access-date=29 December 2018 |date=21 December 2018 |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

==Scientific research==
Spence was a scientific researcher in [[plant virus|plant virology]] at [[Horticulture Research International]] and [[Food and Environment Research Agency|Fera]]. She has researched viral diseases of crops and horticulture both in Africa and the UK.

Her research into viral diseases of crops in Africa has included investigations into the pathogenicity of [[bean common mosaic virus]]<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Spence | first1 =NJ | last2 =Walky| first2 =DGA| title =Variation for pathogenicity among isolates of bean common mosaic virus in Africa and a reinterpretation of the genetic relationship between cultivars of Phaseolus vulgaris and pathotypes of BCMV | journal =Plant Pathology | volume =44 | issue =3 | pages =527–546 |year =1995 | doi = 10.1111/j.1365-3059.1995.tb01675.x| bibcode =1995PPath..44..527S }}</ref> and its occurrence in [[legumes]] in Uganda.<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Sengooba | first1 =TN |last2 =Spence| first2 =NJ| last3 =Walkey| first3=DGA| last4 =Allen| first4=DJ| last5 =Lana| first5 =AF | title =The occurrence of bean common mosaic necrosis virus in wild and forage legumes in Uganda | journal =Plant Pathology | volume =46 | issue =1 | pages =95–103 |year =1997 | doi = 10.1046/j.1365-3059.1997.d01-12.x| doi-access =free | bibcode =1997PPath..46...95S }}</ref> She has also published on the [[economic impact]] of [[turnip mosaic virus]], [[cauliflower mosaic virus]] and [[beet mosaic virus]] in Kenya<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Spence | first1 =NJ| last2 =Phiri| first2 =NA| last3 =Hughes| first3 =SL| last4 =Mwaniki| first4 =A| last5 =Simons| first5 =S| last6 =Oduor| first6 =G| last7 = Chacha | first7 =D| last8 =Ndirangu| first8 =S| last9 =Kibata| first9 =GN| last10 =Marris| first10 =GC | title =Economic impact of Turnip mosaic virus, Cauliflower mosaic virus and Beet mosaic virus in three Kenyan vegetables | journal =Plant Pathology | volume =56 | issue =2 | pages =317–323 |year =2006 | doi = 10.1111/j.1365-3059.2006.01498.x}}</ref> and patterns of plant pest introductions into Europe and Africa.<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Waage | first1 =JK | last2 =Woodhall | first2=JW| last3 =Bishop| first3=SJ| last4 =Smith| first4=JJ| last5 =Jones | first5=DR| last6 =Spence| first6=NJ | title =Patterns of plant pest introductions in Europe and Africa | journal =Agricultural Systems | volume =99 | issue =1 | pages =1–5 |year =2008 | doi = 10.1016/j.agsy.2008.08.001| bibcode =2008AgSys..99....1W }}</ref> She was the vegetables technical advisor for the [[Department for International Development]]'s crop protection programme,<ref>{{cite news| title =BSPP News Summer 2001 | publisher =British Society for Plant Pathology |year =2001 | url =http://www.bspp.org.uk/publications/bsppnews/bsppnews39/bsppnews39d.htm }}</ref> leading projects on management of viral diseases in vegetable crops in Kenya<ref>{{cite web |title=Management of Virus Diseases of Vegetable Crops in Kenya – Final Technical Report |last=Spence |first=Nicola |year=2003 |publisher=[[Department for International Development]]}}</ref> and promotion of quality [[kale]] seed in Kenya.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fao.org/docs/eims/upload/agrotech/1996/R8439_FTRPt1.pdf |title=Promotion of quality kale seed in Kenya |access-date=19 May 2018 |last=Spence |first=Nicola |year=2006 |publisher=Department for International Development |archive-date=20 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520193754/http://www.fao.org/docs/eims/upload/agrotech/1996/R8439_FTRPt1.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In UK horticultural systems, Spence has worked on identifying viruses present in ''[[Alstroemeria]]'' crops in the UK,<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Spence | first1 =Nicola J |last2 =Mills| first2 =Peter R|last3 =Barbara|first3 =Dez J| title =A Survey of Viruses of Alstroemeria in the UK and the Characterisation of Carlaviruses Infecting Alstroemeria | journal =European Journal of Plant Pathology | volume =106 | issue =9 | pages =843–847 |year =2000 | doi = 10.1023/A:1008731508023| bibcode =2000EJPP..106..843S }}</ref> as well as isolating and characterising viruses from [[petunia]]<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Spence | first1 =NJ |last2 =Sealy| first2 =I| last3 =Mills | first3 =PR| last4 =Foster| first4= GD | title =Characterisation of a Tobamovirus from Trailing Petunias | journal =European Journal of Plant Pathology | volume =107 | issue =6 | pages =633–638 |year =2001 | doi = 10.1023/A:1017980712521| bibcode =2001EJPP..107..633S }}</ref> and ''[[Cineraria]]''.<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Weekes | first1 =RJ| last2 =Barker| first2 =I| last3 = Spence| first3 =NJ| last4 =O'Neill| first4 =T| last5 =Wood | first5 =KR | title =A UK Isolate of Impatiens Necrotic Spot Virus From Glasshouse-grown Cineraria | journal =Journal of Phytopathology | volume =146 | issue =4 | pages =201–103 |year =1998 | doi = 10.1111/j.1439-0434.1998.tb04680.x}}</ref> Other research included studying the effect of [[pepino mosaic virus]] on tomato [[Crop yield|yield]].<ref>{{cite journal| last1 =Spence | first1 =NJ | last2 =Basham| first2 =J| last3 =Mumford| first3 =RA| last4 =Hayman| first4 =G| last5 =Edmondson| first5 =R| last6 =Jones| first6 =DR | title =Effect of Pepino mosaic virus on the yield and quality of glasshouse-grown tomatoes in the UK | journal =[[Plant Pathology (journal)|Plant Pathology]] | volume =55 | issue =5 | pages =595–606 |year =2006 | doi = 10.1111/j.1365-3059.2006.01406.x| doi-access =free| bibcode =2006PPath..55..595S }}</ref> She was an editor and contributor to the book ''Biotic Interactions in Plant-pathogen Associations''.<ref>{{cite book| last1 =Jeger | first1 =MJ| last2=Spence| first2=NJ | title =Biotic Interactions in Plant-pathogen Associations | publisher =[[Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International|CABI]] | date =2001 | pages =353 | isbn =9780851995120 }}</ref> and she was previously a member of the editorial board for the scientific journal ''[[Plant Pathology (journal)|Plant Pathology]]''.

Spence was appointed chief scientist at Fera in 2009.<ref name=birk />

==Science City York==
In 2009 Spence was appointed the chief executive of [[Science City York]],<ref name=yorkp /> later known as SCY, an organisation supporting the development of science and technology industries in [[York]], England.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scy.co.uk/what-we-do |title=Science City York: what we do |access-date=20 May 2018 |publisher=Science City York}}</ref> In this role, Spence promoted connections between academics and local businesses, managing events such as Venturefest.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.york.ac.uk/news-and-events/features/science-technology-future/ |title=Inspiring science and technology for the future |access-date=19 May 2018 |publisher=[[University of York]]}}</ref> She was key in the development of the concept of the BioVale,<ref name=scy>{{cite news| title =SCY chief takes new role at DEFRA | publisher =The Press | date =17 March 2014 | url =http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/business/news/11082013.SCY_chief_takes_new_role_at_DEFRA/?ref=mac }}</ref> which aims to promote the [[bioeconomy]] in [[Yorkshire and the Humber]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.biovale.org/about-us/ |title=About Us |access-date=20 May 2018 |publisher=BioVale |archive-date=26 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226100641/https://www.biovale.org/about-us/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> She remained in the role for four years, until her appointment as Chief Plant Health Officer.<ref name=scy />

==Chief Plant Health Officer==
Spence took up her post as chief plant health officer in April 2014,<ref name=defra>{{cite web |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/new-chief-plant-health-officer-announced |title=New Chief Plant Health Officer announced |access-date=19 May 2018 |date=10 March 2014 |publisher=[[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|Defra]]}}</ref> and later also became deputy director for plant and bee health.

Spence has made several media appearances in relation to her work at Defra. In April 2016 she appeared on the ''[[Today Programme]]'' to discuss the finding of a resistant [[Fraxinus excelsior|ash]] tree in [[Norfolk]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.treecouncil.org.uk/Press-News/New-research-offers-hope-on-ash-dieback |title=New research offers hope on ash dieback |access-date=19 May 2018 |year=2016 |publisher=[[The Tree Council]]}}</ref> and has also appeared on the [[BBC]]'s ''[[Countryfile]]'' programme. She has also been a guest on ''[[Farming Today]]'' discussing tree diseases in the UK.<ref>{{cite episode| title =Agricultural land purchases, tree diseases, deer| series =[[Farming Today]] | airdate =9 October 2017 }}</ref> In 2016, she was involved in the management of the [[Asian hornet]] outbreak response,<ref>{{cite news| title =Threat to honeybees as Asian hornet's arrival on UK mainland confirmed |work=Adam Vaughan  | date =20 September 2016 | url =https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/sep/20/threat-honeybees-asian-hornet-arrival-uk-confirmed-defra-invasive-species}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| title =Asian killer hornet discovered in Devon posing threat to dwindling native bee populations | work =[[The Independent]] | date =26 September 2017 | url =https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/asian-killer-hornets-devon-bee-populations-british-national-unit-woolacombe-devon-a7968396.html }}</ref> and appeared on the ''[[World at One]]'' to explain Asian hornet biology and the Defra response to the outbreak.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p048lf64?ns_mchannel=social& |title=Search on for the Asian hornet queen |access-date=19 May 2016 |date=21 September 2016 |publisher=[[BBC Radio 4]]}}</ref>

In 2017, in response to the ''[[Xylella fastidiosa]]'' outbreak in several European countries, Spence wrote to the horticulture sector urging them to follow the example of those which had committed not to bring in [[Host (biology)|host]] plants from the affected countries.<ref>{{cite news| title =Europe must step up action against spread of fatal plant disease, says Gove | agency =Press Association | work =[[The Guardian]] | date =8 September 2017 | url =https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2017/sep/08/europe-must-step-up-action-against-spread-fatal-plant-disease-michael-gove }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://data.parliament.uk/DepositedPapers/Files/DEP2018-0101/Act_now_to_keep_the_UK_Xylella_free_letter.pdf |title=Act now to keep the UK ''Xylella'' free |access-date=20 May 2018 |last=Spence |first=Nicola |date=8 September 2017 |publisher=Defra}}</ref> In 2018, she was a guest and speaker at summit examining the risks posed by ''Xylella'' to the horticulture industry hosted by [[Prince Charles]].<ref>{{cite news| title =Calls for horticulture industry alliance to tackle Xylella at Highgrove summit | author =Matthew Appleby | work =Horticulture Week | date =6 February 2018 | url =https://www.hortweek.com/calls-horticulture-industry-alliance-tackle-xylella-highgrove-summit/plant-health/article/1456458 }}</ref>

In May 2018, Spence gave evidence to the [[European Union Committee|EU Select Committee]] on [[Brexit]] and the potential implications for plant health.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://data.parliament.uk/writtenevidence/committeeevidence.svc/evidencedocument/eu-energy-and-environmentsubcommittee/brexit-plant-and-animal-biosecurity/oral/82804.pdf |title=Corrected oral evidence: Brexit: plant and animal biosecurity |access-date=1 June 2018|date=9 May 2018 |publisher=House of Lords}}</ref>

Whilst at Defra, Spence has been active in promoting plant health as a career. In conjunction with the [[Royal Society of Biology]] and Charles Lane at [[Fera Science]], Spence developed the Plant Health Professional Register – a way for those working in the area of plant health to gain a formal recognition of their professional skills and continue their [[professional development]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsb.org.uk/news/14-news/1523-rsb-launches-plant-health-professional-register |title=Society launches Plant Health Professional Register |access-date=19 May 2018 |date=1 June 2016 |publisher=[[Royal Society of Biology]]}}</ref> She worked with [[Harper Adams University]] to put together a course on plant biosecurity, and is a visiting professor at the university.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.harper-adams.ac.uk/news/202978/two-leading-scientists-named-as-visiting-professors |title=Two leading scientists named as visiting professors |access-date=19 May 2018 |date=24 January 2017 |publisher=Harper Adams University}}</ref>

Spence was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2022 New Year Honours]] for services to plant health.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63571|supp=y|page=N9|date=1 January 2022}}</ref>

==Other roles==
Spence has previously served on the [[Board of Trustees]] for [[Kew Gardens]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/reappointments-to-the-board-of-the-royal-botanic-gardens-kew--2 |title=Reappointments to the Board of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date= 19 May 2018 |publisher=[[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|Defra]]}}</ref> She is currently a Trustee for [[The Yorkshire Arboretum]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.yorkshirearboretum.org/trustees-team/ |title=Trustees & Team |access-date=3 June 2018 |publisher=The Yorkshire Arboretum}}</ref> and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology.

Spence is a visiting professor in plant pathology at Harper Adams University. She sits on the [[School governor|board of governors]] at her former school in [[York]], The Mount.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mountschoolyork.co.uk/about-the-mount-school/governing-body/ |title=Governing Body |access-date=19 May 2018 |publisher=The Mount School}}</ref> and a member of the [[University of York]] Court.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.york.ac.uk/about/organisation/governance/court/members/ |title=Constituency and membership of Court |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=University of York}}</ref> She was Vice-President of the [[British Society for Plant Pathology]].<ref name=BSPP /> Spence is chair of the management board of the CONNECTED project that aims to tackle [[Vector (epidemiology)|vector]] borne plant diseases in Africa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.connectedvirus.net/about/management-board/ |title=Prof. Nicola Spence (Chair) |access-date=20 May 2018 |publisher=University of Bristol}}</ref>
